title: CoreXY 3D printer
summary: CoreXY belts, Z screws, a vase that grows
description: A desktop CoreXY FDM printer with a 250 mm build area: a black T-slot frame, MGN12 rails, NEMA 17 motors on two GT2 belts, a bed on two T8 lead screws with floating nuts, and a blue spiral vase printed as a time-lapse while the nozzle runs its rim.
process: Aluminium extrusion cut to length, FDM printing, machined and bought components

difficulty.rationale: A large coupled machine with subassemblies and configurations following t, and full fastener geometry; the couplings stay serial and linear.

standards: HIWIN MGN catalogue (MGN12 rail, MGN12H block)
Gates PowerGrip GT design manual (2MGT, 20-tooth sprocket dimensions, idler minimums)
materials: Aluminium heater block and heat sink, brass nozzle

motion.cycle: one spiral-vase print as a time-lapse: it runs once from the first ring to the finished vase and does not repeat

contacts.why: the lead screw is the motor's shaft (an integrated T8 motor)
the lead screw is the motor's shaft (an integrated T8 motor)
the thread is the joint: the nut's bore and the screw's crest are drawn line-on-line (F-014)

prompt_test.model: Claude Sonnet 5.5, medium effort, through craft3d-cli
prompt_test.result: Built and checked: 0 dof, CoreXY couplings, nozzle on the rim within 0.02 mm and one layer above it at 73 samples, each belt's length constant to 2e-12 mm, bed drop and floats within 0.02 mm, no collisions at 73 samples and at 16 slider corners (13 samples each); the 121-moment collision run was not done. About 65 CLI calls. It guessed the origin, the belt levels, the coupling signs, the Z motors' corners and the slider ranges; these were added to the prompt afterwards, and that wording was not retested.

budget_exception: File size 1.18 MB: the T-slot profile and the MGN parts shared by the frame, gantry, toolhead and bed subassemblies are packed once per subassembly (findings/A-028-part-packed-per-subassembly). Granted by the coordinator up to 1.2 MB.
